title: A generating submodule contains a basis over a semilocal algebra
statement: Let $(D,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a nonzero commutative ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and assume $D/\mathfrak m$ is infinite. Let $D\to E$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $E$ semilocal (it has finitely many maximal ideals), and assume $\mathfrak mE\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(E)$, where $\operatorname{Jac}(E)$ is the intersection of all maximal ideals. Let $P$ be a finite locally free $E$-module of constant rank $r\geq1$, meaning that there is a finite cover of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ by principal opens $D(f_j)$ on which $P_{f_j}\cong E_{f_j}^{\oplus r}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Let $N\subseteq P$ be a $D$-submodule whose $E$-linear span is all of $P$. Then there exist $n_1,\ldots,n_r\in N$ which form an $E$-basis of $P$.

proof.text: Put $k=D/\mathfrak m$. Enumerate the maximal ideals of $E$ as $\mathfrak q_i$ ($i\in I$, with $I$ finite and possibly empty), and put $K_i=E/\mathfrak q_i$, $F_i=P/\mathfrak q_iP$. The radical hypothesis puts $\mathfrak mE$ inside each $\mathfrak q_i$, so $D\to K_i$ factors through $k$. This unital map from a field is injective, since its kernel cannot contain $1$. The residue maps $\pi_i:P\to F_i$ are $D$-linear via these embeddings.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field avoidance and induction; adaptation to constant-rank locally free modules using the local bases in Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free).

proof.text: For every $i$, choose a principal trivializing open $D(f)$ of the given cover containing $\mathfrak q_i$; thus $f\notin\mathfrak q_i$ and $P_f\cong E_f^{\oplus r}$. Apply [lem-a1-local-trivialization-residue-rank] to get $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\cong E_{\mathfrak q_i}^{\oplus r}$ and $\dim_{K_i}F_i=r$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field avoidance and induction; adaptation to constant-rank locally free modules using the local bases in Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free).

proof.text: Restrict each $\pi_i$ to $N$. Its image spans $F_i$ over $K_i$: lift any residue vector to $P$, express that lift as a finite $E$-linear combination of elements of $N$, and reduce the coefficients. Apply [lem-a1-simultaneous-residue-bases] with $Q=N$ and $\rho_i=\pi_i|_N$. The field $k$ is infinite by hypothesis, $I$ is finite, the maps are $D$-linear by step 1, and all target dimensions are $r$ by step 2. Obtain $n_1,\ldots,n_r\in N$ forming bases in every $F_i$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field avoidance and induction; adaptation to constant-rank locally free modules using the local bases in Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free).

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-basis-of-maximal-residue-bases] to these vectors in $P$. Step 2 supplies the rank-$r$ maximal localizations and step 3 supplies the prescribed residue bases. Hence $E^{\oplus r}\to P$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum a_jn_j$, is bijective, giving the required $E$-basis with every vector in $N$. If $E=0$, the maximal spectrum is empty and these same assertions give the isomorphism $E^{\oplus r}\cong P=0$.
